case_title: GHUSABHAI RAISANGBHAI CHORASIYA & ORS. v. STATE OF GUJARAT
neutral_facts: The deceased, a woman, married to the accused, a man, had a child with him. The accused had an extramarital affair with another woman. The deceased and the accused lived separately in the same house. The deceased informed her sister that there was a separation and that she would return to her parental home after the Holi festival. The deceased committed suicide. The prosecution alleged that the accused and his relatives subjected the deceased to cruelty, which led to her suicide. The prosecution presented evidence, including witness statements and documents, to support the claim of cruelty. The accused denied involvement and claimed that the deceased had divorced him. The trial court convicted the accused under Sections 498A, 306, 201, and 114 of the IPC. The High Court upheld the conviction. The Supreme Court reviewed the case and found that the evidence did not establish the necessary level of cruelty to support the conviction under Section 498A. The Court also found that the evidence against the other accused was insufficient to sustain their conviction. The Supreme Court acquitted all the accused.
